title: Sound simulation of the harp focus on the finger-string interaction.
author: Luana Marinho do Nascimento
abstract: The harp is a string instrument constituted by several strings attached to a vibrating structure, producing an efficient sound propagation. The component of this structure directly connected to the strings, namely the soundboard, has a complex design and can be made from different materials. The sound response of the harp depends on the values of the displacement and velocity of the excited string, at instant it is released to oscillate freely. Those initial conditions for the vibration movement results from the imposed excitation as well as on the physical interaction between the string and the finger of the player. For that reason, this scientific project intends to describe the physical properties of this interaction and to model the behaviour of the string, in order to output the fields of velocity and displacement of the string at the instant of imminent free oscillation movement. To achieve those goals, a theoretical description of the interaction phenomenon in addition to a method for fitting experimental data will be proposed. The resultant values of this project would be further used in the sound synthesis by a superposition model.
